hou-universe.title: HOU Universe
hou-universe.description: A personal technical portfolio website with a cosmic theme — built from scratch with modern web technologies to create a personal brand showcase space.
hou-universe.fullDescription: HOU Universe is my personal technical portfolio website, creating a personal brand showcase space with a cosmic theme. The platform is built on Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript strict mode, blending Tailwind CSS with glassmorphism design language to create a unified visual system of deep black + cool white + light blue accents. From starfield particle backgrounds to mouse glow interactions, from typewriter animations to scroll-driven parallax effects, every detail pursues excellence. The platform covers project showcases, skill visualization, guestbook & contact, bilingual support (zh-CN/en), and visitor statistics, all with full responsive adaptation.
hou-universe.background: As a personal developer, I needed a platform to centrally showcase technical capabilities, project outcomes, and learning journey. HOU Universe was born — it is not only a portfolio website but also a showcase space for my personal technical brand. With a deep-space cosmic visual theme, the entire development process was driven by AI-engineering workflows, compressing weeks of traditional work into days while maintaining high code standards and user experience.
coreFeatures: Project portfolio: curated project cards with cover images, tech tags, and download buttons; detail pages with complete technical solutions and update log timelines
Skill visualization: tiered progress bars displaying four skill categories (Programming Languages / Databases / Core Competencies / AI Engineering), with scroll-triggered percentage growth animations
Guestbook & contact: Netlify Forms integrated guestbook wall and contact form, supporting file attachment uploads with automatic email notifications
Bilingual support: complete i18n solution based on i18next covering all site text content in zh-CN and en
Visitor statistics: real-time visitor counter and page view tracking with persistent data storage
Deep space theme: three-layer parallax starfield, 3D planet model, mouse glow tracking, glassmorphism design language, fully responsive
hou-universe.techSolution: The frontend is built on Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript strict mode for type safety. Styling uses Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui (Base UI) component system with CSS custom properties for unified dark theme tokens. Framer Motion manages page transitions, scroll-triggered entries, and interaction feedback. Canvas API powers the high-performance starfield particle system, while Three.js (React Three Fiber) drives the 3D planet element. Internationalization is based on i18next + react-i18next supporting zh-CN / en. The build outputs a fully static site (output: export), deployed on Netlify with AI-engineering workflows (Claude Code + Harness methodology) driving the entire development process.

shuatiapp-pro-max.title: Code Practice PRO MAX
shuatiapp-pro-max.description: An online coding practice platform for programming learners, solving the pain points of difficult bulk question import and inefficient mistake review — supporting dual-mode import via text paste and file upload.
shuatiapp-pro-max.fullDescription: Code Practice PRO MAX is an online coding practice platform for programming learners, focused on solving the pain points of difficult bulk question import and inefficient mistake review. It supports dual-mode bulk import via text paste and file upload, with intelligent format recognition that automatically parses questions, options, and answers. The mistake notebook auto-collects wrong answers, favorites allow easy review of key questions, and the targeted practice module supports category-specific training. Answer timing and accuracy statistics help students track learning progress in real-time, while the data analytics dashboard visually presents practice trends. The frontend is built with vanilla JavaScript, backend based on Node.js + Express, with MySQL storing question banks and user data.
shuatiapp-pro-max.background: In programming learning, practice is the core means of reinforcing knowledge, but traditional approaches suffer from scattered question sources, inconvenient mistake management, and difficulty tracking learning progress. Code Practice PRO MAX was created to address these pain points, providing a one-stop practice experience from question import to data analysis, solving the core problems of difficult bulk import and inefficient mistake review.
coreFeatures: Dual-mode bulk import: supports text paste and file upload (CSV/JSON), with intelligent format recognition automatically parsing questions, options, and correct answers, significantly reducing entry costs
Auto mistake collection: wrong answers automatically added to the mistake notebook, supporting category filtering and date sorting for targeted review of weak areas
Favorites module: manually bookmark key question types and high-frequency exam topics, quickly review core questions, avoiding information overload
Targeted practice: category-specific training by data structures, algorithms, databases, etc., with flexible selection of practice scope and question volume
Answer timing system: automatic per-question timing recording response duration, helping develop time management awareness and exam pacing
Accuracy & data statistics: accuracy trends, category mastery radar charts, daily practice volume bar charts, visually presenting learning progress
shuatiapp-pro-max.techSolution: The frontend is built with vanilla JavaScript + HTML5 + CSS3 without heavy frameworks, ensuring loading speed and compatibility. The backend is based on Node.js + Express framework providing RESTful API interfaces, with a frontend-backend separated architecture and form validation ensuring data integrity. MySQL database stores question banks, user data, and learning records with data persistence. The intelligent format recognition module uses regex + rule engine to parse multiple question formats (plain text, CSV, JSON), automatically mapping to standard data structures. Answer timing is based on frontend timestamp recording, while accuracy statistics are computed in real-time via SQL aggregate queries. The overall architecture is lightweight and modular for easy future extension.
highlights: Dual-mode import reduces entry cost: text paste + file upload dual channels, intelligent format recognition with >95% accuracy covering mainstream practice platform export formats
Three-dimensional practice loop: auto mistake collection + key question favorites + category-specific training, building a complete practice feedback loop across three dimensions
Data visualization for progress tracking: accuracy trends, category mastery, and practice volume trends — three chart types helping students precisely identify weak areas
Modular extensible architecture: frontend static resource caching ensures offline usability; mistake notebook, favorites, and targeted practice modules are independently decoupled

rice-yield-prediction.title: Rice Yield Prediction and Feature Impact Analysis via Multi-Algorithm Comparison
rice-yield-prediction.description: Independent course project on precision-agriculture yield estimation. Using the UCI rice variety dataset (2,790 samples, 45 mixed features), it builds and compares SVR, MLP, and CART regression models; the best CART model reaches R² = 0.9918.
rice-yield-prediction.fullDescription: This independent course project addresses yield estimation for precision agriculture. Starting from the UCI rice variety dataset (2,790 samples, 45 mixed features), the pipeline performs missing-value checks, outlier treatment, categorical encoding, and algorithm-specific standardization, then builds SVR, MLP, and CART regression models tuned with 5-fold cross-validation and grid search. Models are compared on MSE, RMSE, MAE, and R², with residual analysis used to check for systematic bias. Feature-importance analysis identifies five key factors, including seedling area and potassium fertilizer application, which together explain 99.96% of yield variance. The project concludes with production recommendations across seedling management, precise fertilization, pest and disease control, and population regulation. All results are offline course-project experiments and do not imply deployment on a real farm.
rice-yield-prediction.background: Precision agriculture needs data-driven yield estimates. The project uses the public UCI rice variety dataset (2,790 samples, 45 mixed features) to build and compare regression models, identify the main drivers of yield, and translate the findings into practical production guidance.
coreFeatures: End-to-end data modeling: missing-value checks, outlier treatment, categorical encoding, and algorithm-specific standardization; SVR, MLP, and CART models tuned with 5-fold cross-validation and grid search, with the best CART model reaching R² = 0.9918.

Multi-metric evaluation: MSE, RMSE, MAE, and R² comparison across all three algorithms, with residual analysis confirming no systematic bias; feature-importance analysis identifies five key factors, including seedling area and potassium fertilizer use, explaining 99.96% of yield variance.
Actionable conclusions: production recommendations across seedling management, precise fertilization, pest and disease control, and population regulation, documented in a complete research report.

campus-stationery-ecommerce.title: Campus Stationery E-Commerce System Based on MVC Architecture
campus-stationery-ecommerce.description: Independent practical project: a Java Swing + MySQL desktop e-commerce system for campus stationery, covering browsing, cart, checkout, and an admin back office across a complete MVC-layered architecture.
campus-stationery-ecommerce.fullDescription: This independent practical project is a desktop e-commerce system for campus stationery consumption. Built with Java Swing and MySQL, it covers the full business loop: user browsing, shopping cart, order checkout, and administrator back office. The codebase follows a classic three-layer MVC design separating view, business logic, and data access. A Strategy pattern implements tiered discount calculation, a Singleton encapsulates the database connection utility, and a DAO layer centralizes data access. Order submission uses JDBC transactions for atomicity; stock deduction uses row locking to prevent overselling; queries use PreparedStatement to prevent SQL injection; and user passwords are stored as MD5 digests. The project includes full-scenario functional testing and fixes for null-pointer issues in historical data and discount-strategy matching errors. It is a local desktop course project and has not been commercially deployed; MD5 is a legacy implementation and has not been upgraded to a modern password-hashing scheme.
campus-stationery-ecommerce.background: A desktop e-commerce system for campus stationery, built with Java Swing + MySQL. The project covers user browsing, cart, checkout, and an administrator back office, and practices layered software design and design patterns.
coreFeatures: Classic MVC three-layer architecture separating view, business logic, and data access; Strategy pattern for tiered discounts, Singleton for database connections, and DAO for data access.

Four core modules: multi-role users, full product lifecycle management, real-time cart settlement, and transactional order submission; JDBC transactions preserve order atomicity and row locking prevents stock overselling.

Security and testing: PreparedStatement prevents SQL injection and MD5 digests store passwords; full-scenario testing fixes null-pointer issues in historical data and discount-strategy matching errors.
campus-stationery-ecommerce.techSolution: The system uses Java Swing for the desktop UI and MySQL for users, products, carts, and orders, organized in a three-layer MVC architecture. Order submission uses JDBC transactions for atomicity, stock deduction uses row locking to avoid overselling, data access goes through a DAO layer, and SQL uses PreparedStatement parameters. Passwords are stored as MD5 digests (a legacy course-project implementation, not upgraded to a modern password-hashing scheme). Tiered discounts use the Strategy pattern. The system is a local desktop project and has not been commercially deployed.

JDBC transactions + row locking for order atomicity and stock consistency
PreparedStatement parameterized queries prevent SQL injection
Complete business loop from browsing and cart to checkout and admin back office

publicResearch.title: Small model, bounded claims
publicResearch.subtitle: A public record of what a 1.13M-parameter MiniMind can and cannot learn — including the experiments that failed, the audits that weakened earlier conclusions, and the work still blocked.
publicResearch.disclaimer: Every claim below is scoped to a closed-domain fact set, author-written prompts, and a single small model. None of it is a claim of general language understanding.

phases.title: Research log
phases.intro: Thirteen phases, in order. Negative and inconclusive results are kept rather than hidden.

p113.question: Can chat SFT teach a 1.13M-parameter model to answer held-out chat questions?
p113.result: All three arms scored 0/27 exact match. The SFT arm learned EOS stopping (18/27) but produced no correct answers.
p113.limitation: Single seed, 132 author-written samples. 0/27 cannot separate data, capacity, optimization, or evaluation strictness.

p114.question: Was Phase 113's failure caused by evaluating an early-stopped snapshot?
p114.result: The final snapshot scored 79/84 on train, 0/21 on validation, and 0/27 on test. Training longer did not help.
p114.limitation: One seed; no capacity or data-size sweep.

p115.question: Can the model answer unseen phrasings of facts it saw in training?
p115.result: Seen phrasing 71/72; new phrasing 25/48; unseen facts 0/24. The baseline scored 0 on all three.
p115.limitation: 12 training facts and one seed. Success may depend on vocabulary shared with the training prompts.

p116.question: Does paraphrase transfer reproduce on an independent fact set with three seeds?
p116.result: New phrasing 20/19/19 of 64; seen phrasing 95/96, 96/96, 93/96. Only 9/16 facts were stable across all seeds.
p116.limitation: Fact-level stability falls short of the frozen Grade A rule; unseen facts remain near zero.

p117.question: Is lexical overlap associated with correct answers?
p117.result: Correct answers had higher same-fact Jaccard: pooled +0.0677 (point-biserial 0.282) in Phase 116 and +0.0598 in Phase 115.
p117.limitation: Jaccard is not a complete measure of semantic overlap, and the analysis is correlational.

h118.question: With overlap controlled, are high-overlap prompts easier?
h118.limitation: Low-overlap prompts were 5.69 formatted tokens longer, a confound addressed in H119.

h119.question: Does the overlap effect survive matching prompt length and directness?
h119.result: High 70/96 vs low 23/96; D +48.96 pp, 95% CI [+36.46, +61.46]. The strictest sensitivity had only 2 clusters and D = 0.
h119.limitation: H120 reclassified the result because the frozen rule required the strictest sensitivity to stay positive.

h120.question: Was H119's SUPPORTED label actually derived from its frozen decision rule?
h120.result: Criteria C1–C5 passed; C6 failed when the strictest sensitivity gave D = 0. The main estimate was unchanged.
h120.limitation: The issue is label derivation and an underpowered sensitivity analysis, not a reversed effect.

h121.question: Can paraphrase augmentation improve exact match on low-overlap held-out prompts?
h121.result: Low overlap 23/96 → 42/96; Δ +19.79 pp, 95% CI [+9.38, +31.25]; against the matched control +18.75 pp.
h121.limitation: 16 fact clusters, three batch-order seeds, fixed 144 steps. PROMISING is a preregistered label, not external confirmation.

h122.question: Can the validation metric be used to select checkpoints for this task?
h122.result: No code bug. Validation used 4 unseen facts and scored 0/24 EM at all 12 checkpoints; the loss-best step 96 fit only 51–55/96 training probes, versus 93–96/96 at the final step.
h122.limitation: The validation set measured a different target. Early stopping on it is not valid for this task.

h123.question: With task-aligned selection, does augmentation beat the control on a one-shot final set?
h123.result: All six runs selected step 144. Final evaluation was blocked by one prompt at 89 > 88 tokens; no confirmatory endpoint was produced.
h123.limitation: An instrumentation block, not a result. Phase 123-v2 repaired exactly one prompt's token count.

h123v2.question: After repairing only that prompt's token count, what does the one-shot final evaluation show?
h123v2.result: Intervention 117/288 vs control 92/288; D +0.0868, 95% CI [+0.0486, +0.1354]; 13/16 facts positive, 3 zero, 0 negative.
h123v2.limitation: High-overlap and English subgroup CIs cross zero; 16 clusters; one 1.13M model. This is not a confirmatory or publication-grade result.

p124.question: Can the augmentation effect replicate on entirely new facts with a two-stage within-fact design?
p124.result: No formal facts, prompts, training, evaluation, or bootstrap have run. Gate A is READY FOR HUMAN REVIEW; Gates B and C are BLOCKED; Gate D is DESIGN-LEVEL ONLY; Gate E is PARTIAL.
p124.limitation: The design prohibits training until every gate passes. The next step is human review, not data generation.

findings.title: What the evidence supports
findings.intro: Four findings that survive the limitations below.

memory.title: Closed-domain memory is reliable
memory.body: Train fit reached 79/84; seen-phrasing accuracy was 71/72 in Phase 115 and 93–96/96 in Phase 116. The model can memorize the trained mapping.

paraphrase.title: Paraphrase transfer is partial
paraphrase.body: New phrasings scored 25/48 in Phase 115 and 19–20/64 in Phase 116. Only 9/16 facts were stable across all three seeds.

unseen.title: Unseen facts do not transfer
unseen.body: Phase 115 scored 0/24 on unseen facts; Phase 116 stayed near zero. These results are not open-domain generalization.

augmentation.title: Augmentation is promising, not confirmed
augmentation.body: Phase 123-v2 measured +8.68 pp across 16 fact clusters, with an independent audit at PASS WITH CAVEATS.

limitations.title: Limits and open questions
limitations.intro: These constraints apply to every result on this page.
items: Scale: 1.13M parameters, byte-level BPE, vocabulary 300, 16 fact clusters, 3 batch-order seeds, and 144 steps. Nothing here extrapolates to larger models or natural traffic.
Few clusters: 16 fact-level clusters make bootstrap intervals coarse. They are uncertainty ranges, not precise significance tests.
Seeds are not independent: all three share one initialization; only DataLoader order changes.
Single prompt author: the prompts and paraphrases were written by one author, so coverage of real user phrasing is unknown.
Overlap is a proxy: lexical Jaccard is not semantic overlap, and matched prompts still differ in syntax, register, and reasoning route.
PROMISING is a preregistered label: H121 and Phase 123-v2 are not independent replications or publication-grade confirmation.
Phase 124 has no formal data: the directory contains empty placeholders, not a candidate fact set.

roadmap.title: What comes next
roadmap.intro: Three preregistered directions, in priority order. All are planned; none has started.

independent-facts.title: Independent fact replication
independent-facts.body: Run the same recipe on at least 32 newly written facts with 3 seeds, and keep the final prompts unseen until selection is frozen.

english-coverage.title: English coverage and balance
english-coverage.body: Increase and diversify English paraphrases while keeping total presentations and steps matched; test that Chinese does not regress.

author-generalization.title: Author generalization
author-generalization.body: Replace single-author prompts with an independent author or a frozen template library to test whether the effect is a prompt-style artifact.

phase124.title: Phase 124-A1 gate status
phase124.intro: A design-only replication. No training is permitted until all five gates pass.
phase124.note: Gate E detail: instrument checks pass; frozen-data replay is blocked because no formal data or manifest exists. Source: Phase 124 decision-gate audit.

source.title: Source code
source.body: The training, evaluation, and audit code is not yet published as a public repository. No source link is shown rather than pointing to an unverified repository.

architecture.title: Why These Modules Exist
architecture.description: Each component in MiniMind solves a specific problem. Understanding why each exists is the first step to understanding how they work together.

tokenizer.title: Tokenizer — Text to Numbers
tokenizer.description: Computers don't understand text directly. The Tokenizer converts raw character sequences into discrete token IDs — the only representation the model can process. MiniMind uses a V1 Word Tokenizer that splits on whitespace, maps words to vocabulary indices, and supports encode/decode round-trips.

embedding.title: Embedding — Discrete to Continuous
embedding.description: Token IDs are meaningless integers. The Embedding layer maps each token ID to a dense vector of learnable parameters — placing semantically similar tokens near each other in a continuous vector space. This is the model's first step toward understanding meaning.

transformer.title: Transformer — Layer by Layer Processing
transformer.description: The Transformer block is the engine. Each layer applies multi-head self-attention (tokens look at each other), followed by a feed-forward network (per-token processing), with residual connections and layer normalization ensuring stable, deep training. Stacking multiple layers lets the model build increasingly abstract representations.

sampling.labDescription: The same logits, scaled by different temperatures. Lower temperatures sharpen the distribution (high-confidence tokens dominate); higher temperatures flatten it (more diverse candidates become viable).
sampling.compareFooter: T → 0: distribution collapses to argmax (greedy, deterministic). T = 1: raw softmax, no modification. T → ∞: distribution approaches uniform (maximum entropy, fully random). Temperature controls the exploration-exploitation trade-off in autoregressive generation.
sampling.fullVectorFooter: All {{vocab}} token probabilities. Higher bars = more likely to be sampled at T={{temp}}.
